posts.subject: Lenovo Legion 27QD-10 – Automatic Brightness Reduction and Firmware Inquiry
posts.author: JohnDoe143
posts.message_html:
I am experiencing an intermittent automatic brightness reduction issue with my Lenovo Legion 27QD-10 monitor and would like to know whether this is a known issue and whether a firmware update is available to resolve it. 

Problem description:

When displaying dark content, the monitor's brightness sometimes decreases noticeably and remains reduced even after the on-screen content changes. This occurs particularly frequently when using dark mode in the ChatGPT web interface.

The brightness can temporarily be restored by increasing or decreasing the brightness setting using the monitor's OSD menu. However, the issue may occur again later.

On one occasion, opening an image with a white background coincided with the brightness returning to normal, accompanied by a brief screen flicker. However, I have been unable to reproduce this behavior consistently, so it may have been coincidental.

Troubleshooting already performed:

Changed the monitor's refresh rate, without resolving the issue.
Disabled NVIDIA G-SYNC, without resolving the issue.


The issue appears to involve the monitor's brightness behavior rather than a simple brightness setting, since manually changing the brightness temporarily restores the expected image brightness.

posts.subject: Re:Lenovo Legion 27QD-10 – Automatic Brightness Reduction and Firmware Inquiry
posts.author: Adriel_lenovo
posts.message_html:
Hello and welcome to the Lenovo Community JohnDoe143,

I understand you’re seeing intermittent dimming on your Legion 27QD-10 monitor. May I ask, when did it start to happen? Were there any changes that's been made to the device before it occur?

Since you’ve already ruled out refresh-rate changes and NVIDIA G-SYNC, so the next step is to focus on the monitor’s own image-processing and firmware path. Intermittent dimming on dark content, especially when brightness returns after changing an OSD setting, usually points to a monitor-side dynamic brightness or content-adaptive behavior rather than a simple Windows or GPU setting.

Please try this in order:
1) Open the monitor OSD and reset picture-related settings to factory defaults if you have not done that yet.
2) In the OSD, disable any options related to dynamic contrast, smart image, adaptive brightness, local dimming, HDR, auto black level, or any content-adaptive picture enhancement if present.
3) Set the monitor to a standard picture mode rather than gaming/movie/HDR-style presets, then test again with dark content.
4) If HDR is enabled in Windows, turn HDR off temporarily and retest, since HDR tone behavior can sometimes look like brightness pumping.
5) Test with a different connection path if available, for example a different DisplayPort cable, HDMI, or another source device, to confirm whether the behavior follows the monitor itself.
6) Power the monitor off completely, unplug it from AC power for at least 2 minutes, reconnect it, and test again.
7) Check the monitor support page for your exact Legion 27QD-10 for any available firmware or driver/update utility by clicking here. If an update is listed, install only the one specifically intended for your exact monitor model and follow the included instructions carefully. If no firmware is posted, there may not be a customer-applied firmware release available at this time.

Please inform us of the results.

Thanks,
Adriel_Lenovo

posts.subject: Re:Lenovo Legion 27QD-10 – автоматическое снижение яркости и запрос о прошивке
posts.author: JohnDoe143
posts.message_html:
None of the recommended steps resolved the issue. However, I have identified a possible connection between the brightness problem and my dual-monitor setup when DSC is enabled.

The issue appears to be resolved, at least for now, by lowering the refresh rate of my secondary monitor (not the Lenovo Legion 27QD-10).


In the NVIDIA Control Panel, I changed the resolution mode for the second monitor from "PC" to "Ultra HD, HD, SD." Under the "PC" category, the 1920 × 1080 resolution was only available at 144 Hz, whereas under the "Ultra HD, HD, SD" category, the maximum refresh rate available for this monitor was 120 Hz. After making this change, the brightness issue stopped occurring during my tests.





I tested the following scenarios:

1. Only the Lenovo Legion 27QD-10 monitor is connected and active.

The monitor works without the brightness issue, with DSC enabled. DSC is required to use the monitor at 240 Hz in my configuration.

2. I disconnect the secondary monitor's cable from the GPU and reconnect it.

DSC becomes enabled automatically, and the brightness issue does not occur again until I restart the computer. This remains true even when the secondary monitor is configured to use the PC 1920 × 1080 at 144 Hz mode in the NVIDIA Control Panel.

3. I disable DSC on the Legion 27QD-10 monitor.

This leads to issues when using a dual-monitor setup, regardless of the display settings in use. In my case, the entire desktop shifts from the Lenovo Legion 27QD-10 to the second monitor, and I am no longer able to move the mouse cursor onto the Lenovo screen.


Based on the behavior described in scenario 2, I suspect there may be a firmware or software-related issue involving DSC and multi-monitor operation. 

My secondary monitor is a BenQ EX2510, which supports 144 Hz only over DisplayPort. This might be relevant to the issue. It is likely for this reason that, under the "PC" category for a 1920 × 1080 resolution, only the 144Hz refresh rate is available.

posts.author: JohnDoe143
posts.message_html:
Update:
The issue is not related to DSC. The strange behavior I observed in a dual-monitor setup without DSC was actually caused by the monitor positioning settings getting reset; the system began detecting my secondary monitor on the left instead of the right, which prevented me from moving the cursor over to the primary monitor.
The issue can be reproduced - for instance, when loading the ChatGPT website, white pixels flash briefly on the screen, followed by black pixels (when using the dark theme). This does not occur when using the light theme.

All settings that could trigger automatic brightness adjustments on the monitor have been disabled, so the problem likely lies within the monitor's own firmware/software.

posts.subject: Re:Lenovo Legion 27QD-10 – Automatic Brightness Reduction and Firmware Inquiry
posts.author: Adriel_lenovo
posts.message_html:
Thanks for getting back to us JohnDoe143,

Since you already ruled out refresh rate changes, G-SYNC, DSC, and disabled the monitor settings that can trigger automatic brightness changes, the behavior you describe points to the monitor reacting incorrectly to certain content transitions, especially dark-to-bright or bright-to-dark changes. The brief flicker and the fact that changing brightness in the OSD temporarily restores normal luminance also suggest the issue is likely tied to the monitor’s internal image/brightness control rather than a Windows brightness setting.

Please try this one clean test path:
1. Open the monitor OSD and perform a factory reset.
2. After the reset, leave any dynamic contrast, local dimming, HDR, adaptive brightness, smart energy saving, or similar picture enhancement options turned off.
3. Test with HDR disabled in Windows first.
4. If you are using DisplayPort, test with a different certified DP cable; if possible, also test once over HDMI to see whether the behavior changes.
5. Test the monitor on another system or another video source with the same dark-content scenario.
6. If the issue appears across inputs or systems, note the exact monitor firmware version shown in the OSD information menu if available.

If the monitor continues to dim in the same way after a factory reset and across another cable/input/source, treat this as a monitor firmware issue or hardware-level display control issue. With this, you can contact the technical support in your region instead at 386-1-4755-559 for further assistance. Their operating hours are 8:00-16:00 Monday - Friday. Provide them its serial number so they can also review its warranty info.

Best regards,
Adriel_Lenovo
